title: Choose a class decorator, subclass hook, or metaclass
sources: Python 3.14 Language Reference: data model, customizing class creation and metaclasses; Python 3.14 Descriptor HOWTO; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: Descriptors, decorators, metaclasses, class creation hooks — advanced/internals
whyItMatters: Frameworks often attach metadata or validate subclasses as classes are created. Knowing the simpler hooks first helps you read those frameworks without adding invisible complexity to an ordinary application.
simpleExplanation: A class decorator is a function that receives a completed class and returns a class (possibly the same one); it is useful for explicit one-class customization. __init_subclass__ runs when a subclass is created and is useful for a base class's small subclass policy. A metaclass controls class-object creation more broadly; the default is type. Use a custom metaclass only when simpler tools cannot express the rule, because metaclass conflicts and hidden creation behavior can complicate inheritance. A descriptor is different: an object stored on the class that manages attribute access via __get__, __set__ or __delete__; __set_name__ can learn its assigned field name during class creation. A simple property is usually clearer for one field on one class.
mentalModel: A decorator stamps one finished class; a subclass hook runs a base-class checklist for each new child; a metaclass builds the class itself. A descriptor manages a doorway on the finished class.
outcomes: Apply a class decorator that adds safe metadata without replacing the class.
Use __init_subclass__ for a narrow registration policy.
Identify type as the usual metaclass and know when custom metaclasses are disproportionate.
Distinguish class-creation hooks from descriptor-based attribute access.

realWorldExample.scenario: A learning app has a few report types and wants a human-readable label for each.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: A metaclass written solely to add one label can obscure how classes are created and interfere with other frameworks.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Use a decorator for isolated explicit labels, or a small base-class hook if every subclass must register. Escalate to a metaclass only for a genuinely class-construction-level need.

explanation: @labelled receives the completed StudyReport class, sets a deliberately simple display label, and returns that same class.
Report.__init_subclass__ runs when StudyReport is defined and registers it; its cooperative super call leaves room for other class-creation behavior.
type(StudyReport) is the default metaclass type. No custom metaclass is needed for this simple metadata task.
A registry used in a real app needs careful duplicate handling and trusted class sources; this in-memory example keeps scope narrow.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Add a second Report subclass and predict whether the registry gains it. Do not use subclass registration to execute untrusted plugins.

procedure: Decide whether the behavior concerns one explicit class, every subclass of a base, or class-object construction itself.
Use an ordinary class decorator for the first case and return the class.
Use __init_subclass__ for a small inherited rule and call super cooperatively.
Consider a custom metaclass only after the simpler mechanisms fail to express a real requirement.
Keep the registry in memory for learning and test duplicate or untrusted inputs before production use.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing a metaclass merely to attach one label.
commonMistakes.why: It adds invisible class-creation behavior and may conflict with other bases.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use a class decorator or explicit class attribute.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to return cls from a class decorator.
commonMistakes.why: The decorated class name may be replaced with None or another unintended value.
commonMistakes.avoid: Return the class unless replacing it is a deliberate contract.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating subclass registration as safe automatic plugin loading.
commonMistakes.why: Imported code has already executed and may be untrusted; registry contents need governance.
commonMistakes.avoid: Keep plugin discovery and trust decisions explicit and separate.

lab.title: Label and register fictional report classes
lab.safety: Only in-memory classes and strings; no imports from unknown plugins, files or network.
guidedSteps: Make labelled return a nested decorator that sets cls.display_label and returns cls.
Add the new subclass to registry under its class name.
Print the label, sorted registry keys and the name of the default metaclass.
Add a second subclass and observe it register without an explicit decorator.
checks: Outputs Study summary, ['StudyReport'], type before the optional second subclass.
The subclass hook calls super cooperatively.
No custom metaclass or external plugin import is used.
hints: def decorate(cls): cls.display_label = label; return cls
lab.solutionExplanation: The explicit decorator labels one class, and the inherited hook registers the subclass at definition time; the default metaclass remains type.
challenges: Predict registry after defining another Report subclass.
Find the bug if decorate sets the label but forgets return cls.
Experiment: duplicate class names in different scopes and decide what a production registry would need to avoid overwriting.

projectConnection.milestone: Add explicit safe labels and a narrowly scoped report-type registry without a custom metaclass.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Tests verify labelled classes remain usable, subclasses register once, and duplicate naming is handled before any production registry is adopted.

assessment.question: When does __init_subclass__ run?
assessment.answer: When a subclass of the defining base is created.
assessment.explanation: It is a class-creation hook, not an instance initializer.

assessment.question: What is the usual metaclass of an ordinary Python class?
assessment.explanation: A custom metaclass is not needed for simple labeling or registration.

assessment.question: What must a class decorator return here?
assessment.explanation: Otherwise the class name would be rebound to an unintended return value.
